thesis.problem: A grid built on wind and solar needs something firm underneath it that is not gas, and the candidates are few. Fission carries a waste and siting problem Germany has already legislated its way out of, and fusion has spent seventy years being thirty years away. What changed is that the US National Ignition Facility got more energy out of a laser-driven fusion target than went into it, which turned the question from whether the physics works into whether anyone can build a machine that does it several times a second, commercially.
thesis.solution: Focused Energy pursues inertial confinement: banks of extremely powerful lasers compress a fuel pellet until it fuses, repeated at a rate that makes a power station rather than an experiment. It is a spinout of the Technical University of Darmstadt, it bought two of the world's most powerful existing lasers rather than waiting to build them, and it plans its first laser fusion plant on the site of the decommissioned Biblis nuclear station in Hesse by the mid-2030s.

undisclosed.note: No source has published a figure. Gründerszene states the status, not a number.

The crossing round, and no price was attached to it by anyone. Handelsblatt and TechCrunch both cover the round without a valuation, and Gründerszene reports the same round as the moment the company passed a billion, “knackte die Milliarden-Bewertung”, without saying what the figure was. The round is dated here to May, when the company announced it and the German press reported it, not to TechCrunch's June write-up.
